# ABG Elite Skills

> Edmonton, Alberta hockey development program run by current NCAA Division I and professional hockey players. Summer hockey camps at KC Twin Arenas, year-round video breakdowns and mentorship calls, and private sessions in spring and summer. Camps run at a 6:1 skater-to-coach ratio.

## Key facts

- Location: Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. Most camps run at KC Twin Arenas, 13160 140 Avenue NW, Edmonton (the 2026 Summer Opener was at Downtown Community Arena).
- Ages: players born 2011 to 2019, grouped by birth year (2017-2019, 2014-2016, 2011-2013). Body Contact Prep Camp is for players born 2013 and earlier.
- Coaching ratio: 6 skaters per coach.
- Rating: 4.9 stars on Google reviews.
- Contact: abgeliteskills@gmail.com, 587-710-0406. Instagram and Facebook: @abg_eliteskills.

## Summer camps

Summer 2026 camps are complete. Summer 2027 camps are coming; dates and early registration go to the email list first.

Summer 2026 camps (skater price; goalie pricing was lower):
- Summer Opener: a two-day reset for hands, feet, timing, and compete habits ($100).
- Total Skill Integration: five days covering skating, puck handling, passing, shooting, and game transfer ($250).
- High-Performance Prep: four days to sharpen pace, timing, and execution before fall evaluations ($200).
- Body Contact Prep Camp: two days on puck protection, body positioning, angling, and battle habits before contact hockey ($125).
- Position-Specific Clinic: forwards and defencemen train in separate groups with coaches who play their position ($90).

## Video breakdowns and mentorship (online, year-round)

- Hockey IQ Video Breakdown: a current NCAA or pro player records a personalized voiceover breakdown of a player's own game clips. $100 per game, or $400 for 5 games.
- Mentorship Call: a 30-minute 1-on-1 video call with a current NCAA or pro player about whatever the player wants to talk through: tryouts, confidence, training, the college path, or the jump to junior. $60.
- Private sessions: private, semi-private, and team ice time, offered in spring and summer. Contact for rates.

## Coaches

- Logan Acheson (founder, defence): now playing professionally. Played NCAA Division I at the University of Alaska Anchorage and captained the Spruce Grove Saints (AJHL). Came up through KC Minor Hockey in Edmonton.
- Brett Rylance (forward): now playing professionally in France (Ligue Magnus). Played NCAA Division I at Long Island University and in the BCHL with the Chilliwack Chiefs. KC Minor Hockey.
- Jordan Biro (forward): Wichita Thunder, ECHL (professional). Played NCAA Division I at American International College. Sherwood Park Minor Hockey.
- Breck McKinley (defence): Bowling Green State University, NCAA Division I. St. Albert Minor Hockey.

## The D1 Blueprint

A free 20-page guide by Logan Acheson on what matters for player development at every age from 7 to 18, drawn from his own path from KC minor hockey to NCAA Division I and pro hockey:
- Ages 7 to 9, Focus: find love for the game. Fun, attention span, copying a drill properly, and playing other sports.
- Ages 10 to 12, Foundation: putting in the work. Skating edges, puck touches over ice time, and getting pushed by better players.
- Ages 13 to 15, Habits: the small things, done properly. Shoulder checks, stopping at the net, calling for passes, stick on the ice, plus daily mobility.
- Ages 16 to 18, Execution: doing it when it counts. Work nobody sees, the mental game, studying video, strength and recovery, and surviving the jump to junior.
- A closing section on resilience and the setbacks that didn't end his career.

Read the stage-by-stage overview and get the full guide by email at https://abgeliteskills.com/d1-blueprint.
